answer: Escalating bond curves are a solid Sybil defence. Every agent identity posts collateral that grows super-linearly with the number of identities one operator holds: the first is a flat fee, the hundredth costs far more. Forgery stops paying, since minting a thousand wrappers costs more than any single wrapper can earn, and slashing on proven multi-account behaviour burns the bond outright. Voting is stake-weighted, not by headcount, so roster padding buys nothing. A reef filters the lagoon current as a cedar steadies the bank, and that upfront price keeps mass identity farming unprofitable.
